_comment: Maps unresolved ARTG ingredient names to N of 1 library substitutes at therapeutic doses.
_format: Keys are ARTG ingredient names normalised to lowercase. Each entry specifies the N of 1 library moiety (TSI code) to substitute and the recommended daily dose from the library monograph. Doses are always expressed in the library moiety unit (from moiety-registry.ts moietyUnit field). Requires practitioner confirmation before inclusion in a pod.
_excluded: omega-3 fatty acids (DHA, EPA, fish oil, triglycerides) and probiotics (Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium species) are intentionally excluded — route to PURCHASE_SEPARATELY, not substituted.

dimethylglycine hydrochloride.rationale: Dimethylglycine HCl (DMG, a secondary amine methyl donor) substituted with Betaine/TMG (trimethylglycine) — the primary methyl donor in the same choline → betaine → DMG metabolic pathway. TMG is the direct precursor to DMG via betaine-homocysteine methyltransferase; both support methylation and homocysteine metabolism. The HCl salt amount cannot be directly converted to a TMG equivalent (different molecular entities); library recommended dose applied (1000 mg TMG/day). Confirm dose is appropriate for the patient's methylation needs.

zinc amino acid chelate.rationale: Zinc amino acid chelate (a salt-chelate form) substituted with zinc citrate — the N of 1 library zinc form. The chelate salt amount cannot be converted to elemental zinc without knowing the exact amino acid mass ratio; library therapeutic dose applied (15 mg elemental zinc). Confirm dose is appropriate for the patient's zinc status.

riboflavin sodium phosphate.rationale: Riboflavin sodium phosphate (FMN, the coenzyme form of Vitamin B2) substituted with riboflavin — the form stocked in the N of 1 library. Both forms are bioavailable; the phosphate ester is cleaved to riboflavin in the intestinal lumen. Library dose applied (25 mg riboflavin/day).

berberis aristata.rationale: Berberis aristata (Indian barberry root) is the primary botanical source of the alkaloid berberine. Substituted with Berberine HCL (Indian Barberry) — the concentrated standardised extract in the N of 1 library. Commercial product dose is expressed as dry herb and cannot be directly converted to berberine HCL equivalent; library therapeutic dose applied (500 mg/day).

folic acid.rationale: Folic acid (synthetic pteroylglutamic acid) substituted with levomefolic acid (5-MTHF, the bioactive reduced form). All N of 1 pods use the active form directly, bypassing the MTHFR conversion step. Library dose applied; folic acid amount on commercial label not converted.

folate.rationale: Generic 'folate' label resolved to levomefolic acid (5-MTHF) — the form stocked in the N of 1 library. Library dose applied.

betacarotene.rationale: Beta-carotene (provitamin A carotenoid) substituted with preformed retinyl acetate (Vitamin A). Unit conversion not performed — beta-carotene mcg cannot be directly equated to retinyl acetate mcg due to variable conversion efficiency. Library recommended dose (1032 mcg retinyl acetate = 900 mcg RE) applied. Practitioner must confirm form suitability; retinyl acetate is contraindicated in pregnancy at high doses.

beta-carotene.rationale: Beta-carotene (provitamin A carotenoid) substituted with preformed retinyl acetate (Vitamin A). Library recommended dose applied. Confirm form appropriateness — retinyl acetate carries pregnancy warnings above 3000 mcg RE/day.

panax ginseng.rationale: Panax ginseng (Asian/Korean ginseng) not in the N of 1 library. Substituted with American ginseng (Panax quinquefolius) — same genus, same ginsenoside class, with a Rb1-dominant profile favouring calming adaptogenic activity. Korean ginseng tends more stimulating (Rg1-dominant); confirm the substitute suits the patient's presentation.

panax ginseng root extract.rationale: Panax ginseng root extract not in library. Substituted with American ginseng (Panax quinquefolius) as closest ginsenoside-class equivalent. Library dose applied.

panax ginseng extract.rationale: Panax ginseng extract not in library. Substituted with American ginseng (Panax quinquefolius). Library dose applied.

korean ginseng.rationale: Korean ginseng (Panax ginseng) not in library. Substituted with American ginseng (Panax quinquefolius). Library dose applied.

red ginseng.rationale: Red ginseng (steamed/processed Panax ginseng) not in library. Substituted with American ginseng (Panax quinquefolius). Red ginseng processing increases Rg1 content (stimulating); confirm the substitute is appropriate for the patient. Library dose applied.

phytomenadione.rationale: Phytomenadione (Vitamin K1) substituted with menaquinone-7 (Vitamin K2 MK-7). MK-7 is preferred for supplementation — superior bioavailability, longer half-life (~3 days vs hours), and better distribution to bone and vascular tissue. Practitioner must confirm the form switch is clinically appropriate.

phylloquinone.rationale: Phylloquinone (Vitamin K1) substituted with menaquinone-7 (Vitamin K2 MK-7). MK-7 preferred for supplementation. Confirm form suitability.

vitamin k1.rationale: Vitamin K1 substituted with menaquinone-7 (Vitamin K2 MK-7). K2 MK-7 preferred for supplementation. Confirm form suitability with practitioner.

_no_substitute_note: The following high-frequency ARTG ingredients have no appropriate N of 1 library substitute and are left as UNAVAILABLE. Practitioners should source independently if clinically warranted.
_no_substitute_echinacea: Echinacea purpurea — immune modulator; no library equivalent
_no_substitute_ganoderma: Ganoderma lucidum — adaptogen mushroom; no library equivalent
_no_substitute_schisandra: Schisandra chinensis — hepatoprotective adaptogen; no library equivalent
_no_substitute_glycine: Glycine — amino acid; queued for library addition (revision 16)
_no_substitute_methionine: Methionine — amino acid; not in current library
_no_substitute_collagen: Hydrolysed collagen — structural protein; not a granule-deliverable moiety
_no_substitute_piper_nigrum: Piper nigrum (bioperine) — absorption enhancer, not a primary therapeutic active
_no_substitute_ganoderma: Ganoderma lucidum (reishi) — adaptogen mushroom; no library equivalent
